extraction.name: ScienceQA
extraction.description: Science Question Answering (ScienceQA) is a large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question dataset containing 21,208 examples with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. The dataset covers three subjects (natural science, social science, and language science), 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills. Questions include multimodal contexts (images and text), and most are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations that serve as chain-of-thought reasoning demonstrations.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022). arXiv:2209.09513v2 [cs.CL] 17 Oct 2022.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the ScienceQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, and semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems sourced from IXL Learning (https://www.ixl.com/), an online learning platform for K-12 education aligned with California Common Core Content Standards. The dataset includes questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions from elementary and high school science curricula.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed (e.g., questions with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates). If multiple correct answers applied, only one correct answer was kept. Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions so that special structures (tables, lists) are distinguishable from simple text passages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, solutions) were extracted from downloaded science problems using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled. Semi-automated scripts reformatted lectures and solutions. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts. The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20 (12,726 / 4,241 / 4,241 examples respectively).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge introducing background information for solving problems of a similar class. The explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. Annotations were sourced from IXL Learning's existing educational content and further manually revised by experts using a data exploration tool. Human performance was evaluated via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), where workers with a high school or higher degree who passed qualification examples answered test questions. Each question was answered by three different workers. Human evaluation of generated explanations was also conducted via AMT, where workers rated relevance, correctness, and completeness of model-generated explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human performance evaluation, only workers who correctly answered 4 out of 5 exam examples were qualified. For human evaluation of generated explanations, each sample was assigned to 3 workers, and human scores were determined by taking a majority vote. Workers rated explanations on relevance (related to the question), correctness (gives a correct answer and explanation), and completeness (fully explains the answer).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (each question answered by three different AMT workers for human performance study; each explanation rated by 3 workers for human evaluation of generated explanations)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers who hold a high school degree or higher and passed qualification examples (correctly answered 4 out of 5 exam examples).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Image captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 (https://huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) was used to generate captions for images as visual context for language models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://scienceqa.github.io for non-commercial research purposes. The copyright belongs to IXL Learning. The dataset is under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. Any anti-social data points will be removed from the dataset based on feedback.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content. It does not contain any user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: ScienceQA is proposed to diagnose the multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The dataset adheres to the goal of AI for the common good. After careful examination, no improper content such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias was found.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset does not contain harmful social bias according to the authors' examination. The dataset is sourced from California Common Core Content Standards, which may reflect the educational standards and content of that specific curriculum.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal methods fail to achieve satisfactory performance on ScienceQA. Image captions extracted from captioning models lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams. Models fail to understand multimodal inputs and lack domain-specific knowledge for some questions. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of multimodal question answering models; benchmarking multi-hop reasoning and interpretability of AI systems; few-shot and fine-tuning learning with chain-of-thought reasoning; development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems; research on multimodal learning and general artificial intelligence.
